title: Goal-Conditioned Agents that Learn Everything All at Once
claim: Prior methods update each transition toward one goal; ours updates every transition toward all goals at once, extracting maximal information.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, same maze with legend at right
description: Three side-by-side maze diagrams share the same blue trajectory, which loops from the bottom left, around, and up to the top left. Panel (a), Vanilla GCRL, has one orange learning-update line from a transition to the red X commanded goal at the top right. Panel (b), HER, has one orange line from the transition to a goal the trajectory reached later, at the top left. Panel (c), LEO, has many orange curves fanning out from the single transition to a grid of orange goal circles across the maze, so the eye goes to this dense fan first. A legend on the right covers trajectory (blue arrow), transition (blue circle), commanded goal (red X) and learning update (orange line). Black maze walls are the background.
caption: We consider with respect to what goal a given transition in a trajectory is updated to in different GCRL paradigms. In vanilla GCRL ([ref]), the update is done with respect to the goal that was commanded, even if this goal is never satisfied. When using HER ([ref]), the trajectory is relabelled with a goal that was achieved later on, providing a positive signal. With LEO ([ref]), we propose updating jointly with respect to the entire goal set using an efficient update for all-goals learning.
abstract: A goal-conditioned reinforcement learning agent exploring an environment will see a wealth of information throughout a trajectory, most of which is discarded when only performing on-policy updates with respect to the commanded goal. All-goals learning, where each transition is used for learning off-policy with respect to every goal, allows agents to extract maximal information, however it is usually computationally infeasible when done via naive relabelling. This can be overcome by jointly outputting values and actions for every goal at once, allowing for efficient, parallel all-goals updates with a single pass through the network, in a process we call Learning Everything all at Once (LEO). We show that this approach significantly outperforms other methods on goal-conditioned Craftax and is competitive with existing baselines on continuous control environments, while achieving a >250x speed-up compared to all-goals relabelling. We then go on to show that this approach can be made even more powerful by using LEO as a teacher network, rather than a direct actor. We hope that, by unlocking all-goals learning at scale, LEO can serve as a useful tool for RL practitioners in complex environments. We open source our code.
